title: Shell command built from string interpolation in julia — review required
description: Backtick command literals interpolate values into a shell command. A value containing a semicolon or command substitution is parsed by the shell, so the process runs commands the caller did not intend. The rule flags the interpolation; whether the value is externally influenced is a review decision.
remediation: Pass each argument as a separate interpolated element ($(arg)) and avoid shell-string concatenation.
limitation: Lexical: matches interpolation inside a backtick literal; argument-vector calls built from arrays are out of scope.
